---
title: "16 — How much does demographic composition explain the 2025 performance gap?"
output: html_notebook
---

**Research question:**
Is the observed AI/AN-versus-comparison model performance
gap sensitive to differences in age and sex composition?

**Measures:**
2025 survey-weighted AUROC, Brier score, calibration error, and
skill against the frozen historical-prevalence model (a) nationally by group, (b) after
restricting to demographic cells observed in both populations, and (c) after
standardizing both groups to the same age or age-by-sex distribution.

Reweighting by health or socioeconomic predictors could erase
real differences, so these are not included in the common target.

## Initialize and link this analysis to the frozen model run

**Measures:** verifies that this notebook is operating under the current
numbered run and reading the frozen classifier.

```{r setup}
# Find the original RStudio project, regardless of the notebook's working directory.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(current, parent)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

# Read the executable code blocks from existing shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(lines, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(lines) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Incomplete R code chunk in ", path)
        }
        paste(lines[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")
load_module("addon_insight_helpers")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
# Resolve the frozen model run separately from the current output run.
source_run_id <- get_source_run_id()
cat("[ADD-ON] New increment:", run_context$id, "| Original model run:", source_run_id, "\n")
```


## Examine overlap and retain the untouched 2025 predictions

**Measures:** which demographic cells have sufficient AI/AN sample support for
an interpretable comparison, and how many records standardization discards.

```{r define-common-support}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demographic overlap and retained records
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep frozen predictions and identify shared demographic cells using the existing
# helper.
# Audit both row retention and survey-weight retention before interpreting standardized
# metrics.

# Do not retrain the national model or change its frozen 2025 predictions.
source_model <- get_source_model()
selected <- source_model$selection
scored <- data.table::as.data.table(load_source_rds("checkpoints", "07_scored_2025"))
primary <- data.table::copy(scored)[
    cohort %in% primary_groups &
        valid_outcome(FMD) &
        valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT) &
        is.finite(selected_probability)
]
if (!all(primary_groups %in% primary$cohort)) {
    stop("The 2025 source run must contain both comparison groups")
}

# Construct prespecified composition variables from the ORIGINAL survey fields.
primary[, age_cell := as.character(AGE_BAND)]
primary[, age_sex_cell := paste(AGE_BAND, SEX_CLEAN, sep = " | ")]

# Exclude only sparse composition cells (not whole groups or missing categories).
# Missing is retained as a level when enough respondents support the cell.
age_cells <- find_common_cells(primary, "age_cell", min_cell_n = 30L)
age_sex_cells <- find_common_cells(primary, "age_sex_cell", min_cell_n = 30L)
if (!length(age_cells) || !length(age_sex_cells)) {
    stop("Insufficient common demographic support for standardization")
}

support_rows <- list()

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (variable in c("age_cell", "age_sex_cell")) {
    cells <- if (variable == "age_cell") age_cells else age_sex_cells
    audit <- primary[, .(
        total_rows = .N,
        kept_rows = sum(get(variable) %in% cells),
        original_weight = sum(RAW_WEIGHT),
        kept_weight = sum(RAW_WEIGHT[get(variable) %in% cells])
    ), by = cohort]
    audit[, `:=`(
        standardized_on = variable,
        row_fraction_kept = kept_rows / total_rows,
        population_weight_fraction_kept = kept_weight / original_weight,
        common_cells = length(cells)
    )]
    support_rows[[variable]] <- audit
}
support <- data.table::rbindlist(support_rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(support, "16_common_demographic_support")
print(support)
```

## Standardize the model-performance comparison

**Measures:** subgroup metrics if both populations had the same age or
age-by-sex composition. The target is an *equal mixture* of the two groups' weighted
distributions within shared cells, rather than the overwhelmingly larger comparison
group's distribution. This is a constructed target population.

```{r compute-standardized-contrasts}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Restricted and standardized performance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Separate common-support restriction from demographic reweighting.
# Use the shared helper to construct common-composition weights without refitting the
# classifier.

# Start with the full observed 2025 group comparison.
all_metrics <- list(score_groups(
    primary,
    weight_column = "RAW_WEIGHT",
    scenario = "full_original_survey_weights",
    historical_prevalence = selected$training_prevalence
))

# Compare restricted-only and reweighted estimates on identical rows.

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (specification in list(
    list(column = "age_cell", cells = age_cells, label = "age"),
    list(column = "age_sex_cell", cells = age_sex_cells, label = "age_sex")
)) {
    column <- specification$column
    overlap <- primary[get(column) %in% specification$cells]
    all_metrics[[length(all_metrics) + 1L]] <- score_groups(
        overlap,
        weight_column = "RAW_WEIGHT",
        scenario = paste0(specification$label, "_common_support_only"),
        historical_prevalence = selected$training_prevalence
    )

    # Recalculate relative weights using original BRFSS weights within cells.
    standardized <- standardize_weights(
        primary,
        raw_weights = primary$RAW_WEIGHT,
        cell_column = column,
        common_cells = specification$cells
    )
    all_metrics[[length(all_metrics) + 1L]] <- score_groups(
        standardized,
        weight_column = "standardized_weight",
        scenario = paste0(specification$label, "_standardized"),
        historical_prevalence = selected$training_prevalence
    )
    factors <- standardized[, .(
        max_adjustment = max(adjustment),
        min_adjustment = min(adjustment),
        effective_n = sum(standardized_weight)^2 / sum(standardized_weight^2)
    ), by = cohort]
    cat("[DIAGNOSTIC] Weight-factor range for", specification$label, "\n")
    print(factors)
    if (any(factors$max_adjustment > 10)) {
        warning("Large demographic weight factors: interpret composition-adjusted results cautiously")
    }
}

metrics_table <- data.table::rbindlist(all_metrics, use.names = TRUE)
contrasts <- metrics_table[, .(
    ai_an_auc = auc[cohort == primary_groups[1]],
    comparison_auc = auc[cohort == primary_groups[2]],
    ai_an_calibration_error = calibration_error[cohort == primary_groups[1]],
    comparison_calibration_error = calibration_error[cohort == primary_groups[2]],
    ai_an_brier_skill = brier_skill_vs_historical[cohort == primary_groups[1]],
    comparison_brier_skill = brier_skill_vs_historical[cohort == primary_groups[2]]
), by = scenario]
contrasts[, `:=`(
    auc_gap = ai_an_auc - comparison_auc,
    calibration_gap = ai_an_calibration_error - comparison_calibration_error,
    brier_skill_gap = ai_an_brier_skill - comparison_brier_skill
)]


# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(metrics_table, "16_age_sex_composition_group_metrics")
save_table(contrasts, "16_age_sex_composition_gap_comparison")
print(metrics_table)
print(contrasts)
```

## Display the effect of composition standardization

**Measures:** how the point-estimated AUROC gap changes under each common
population definition. The next notebook adds preliminary uncertainty intervals rather
than treating these differences as conclusive.

```{r plot-standardized-gaps}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Composition-sensitivity displays
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Show point-estimated gaps and mean residuals under each comparison definition.
# Changes are descriptive and may include effects of both restriction and reweighting.

# Print plots explicitly so they appear in the HTML notebook as well as PNG.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
gap_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    contrasts,
    ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(scenario, auc_gap), y = auc_gap)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = atg_palette[["mauve"]]) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["burgundy"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Does age/sex standardization alter the 2025 AUROC gap?",
        subtitle = "AI/AN alone minus other single-race; model predictions unchanged",
        x = "Comparison population definition",
        y = "Survey-weighted / standardized AUROC difference",
        caption = "Differences are descriptive; group distributions and common-support exclusions vary."
    )
show_and_save(gap_plot, "16_standardized_auc_gaps", 11, 6)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
calibration_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    metrics_table,
    ggplot2::aes(x = scenario, y = calibration_error, fill = cohort)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["burgundy"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
    atg_scale_fill_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "How calibration changes under common demographic composition",
        x = "Comparison population definition",
        y = "Mean predicted minus observed FMD",
        fill = "Population",
        caption = "Average calibration does not reveal risk-decile miscalibration."
    )
show_and_save(calibration_plot, "16_standardized_calibration", 11, 6)
```
